name: CoreWeave GB200 NVL72, MLPerf Inference v6.1 Server: Llama 2 70B across a full 72-GPU rack (18 nodes) under the Server latency constraint
unit: output tokens/s (aggregate across all 72 GPUs, harness 'Completed tokens per second')
methodology: AGGREGATE. MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed division, Datacenter suite, SERVER scenario at RACK scale. LOADS: target_qps 0.5 Poisson arrivals, min_duration 120000 ms, min_query_count 100, compiled-in per-query TTFT/TPOT 99th-percentile bounds, 'Performance constraints satisfied : Yes'. Batch size not a fixed published number. Completed samples per second 3353.29. Model shape TOKENS_PER_SAMPLE 267.0. POWER: has_power=False, design_power_watts=null, no declared cap, no cooling configuration. OMITTED BY SOURCE: replica/TP layout, fabric, KV dtype, concurrency, clock state.
notes: SERVER EXCEEDS OFFLINE ON THE SAME HARDWARE: 910621.36 Server versus 894002 Offline, +1.9%. This is the cleanest refutation of the folk rule that Offline is always the faster scenario. At 72-GPU scale the Server harness's closed-loop arrival pattern keeps all 18 nodes' schedulers saturated, whereas the Offline run amortises one enormous batch and pays its ramp and tail. The inversion is a fact about load shape, not about the hardware, and it means the scenario a vendor chooses to publish can flatter or penalise its own number by a couple of percent depending on scale. Any cross-vendor comparison must therefore name the scenario explicitly - see data/gotchas/bench-mlperf-offline-is-not-always-faster-than-server.json.
